khai.tagline: Social comparison as process: how a persona evaluates their own opinions and abilities by measuring against others -- across the upward, downward, and similar forms.

card.wire: Attaches at Process. The root (process_comparison.md) declares social comparison as Festinger's account: a persona has a drive to evaluate their opinions and abilities, and where no objective standard is at hand, they measure against other people -- so the self is known by where it stands relative to others rather than in the absolute. The law makes the standing of others the yardstick of the self: what a persona judges themselves to be is read off the gap between themselves and those they compare with.
card.issue: Three ways the measuring runs. Upward: comparison with those who are better off or more able -- which informs and can inspire the reach to improve, but can also threaten, breeding inadequacy or envy when the gap is large and the domain matters. Downward: comparison with those who are worse off -- which enhances the self, the persona feeling better by the contrast, a defense drawn on most under threat. Similar: the selection of the comparison target -- a persona compares most tellingly with those like themselves, because only a similar other yields a diagnostic read on where they truly stand.
card.require: Two altitudes hold the engine. The law: declared once in the project's Instructions Knowledge chapter, linking the root. The link: each persona links, under Projection, the form the moment runs -- and therefore how the self is being measured, by a look upward that informs or threatens, a look downward that enhances, or the choice of a similar other that makes the read diagnostic.
card.enforce: Structure is checked; coherence is judged. The kit verifies the floor: the law is declared and each persona links a real form of comparison. Whether the measuring is true to the scene -- a genuine self-evaluation against a real other, the upward or the downward or the similar read right, the self known by the gap -- is semantic, taught and reviewed, never failed by the suite.
card.setup: Declare the law in the Instructions Knowledge chapter, linking the root. Then give the persona its form under Projection. Read it as a persona measuring their own opinions or abilities against others -- the look upward, the look downward, the similar other chosen as yardstick -- never as the emotion the comparison provokes, nor as the standing itself, nor as the global self-attitude. Delegate the pain at another's superiority to the envy engine, the persona's rank in an order to the status engine, the resting global self-attitude to the self-esteem engine, and the catalog of comparison tilts held as static positions to the bias engine.
